activity_context.topic_title: Expressing Rational Functions as Sums of Partial Fractions

feedback.problem:
Given that

$$
\frac{-2x-9}{(x+3)x}=\frac{1}{(x+3)}+\frac{B}{x},
$$

what is the value of $B?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Our task is to find $B$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-2x-9}{(x+3)x}=\frac{1}{(x+3)}+\frac{B}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying both sides by $(x+3)x$ gives

$$
-2x-9=x+B(x+3).
$$

For $x=0$, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}-2(0)-9 & =0+B(0+3) \\ -9 & =3B \\ B & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$
